how_we_chose: Parties appear if they have a sitting MP or average 2% or more in recent nationwide polls, and publish policies on their own website.
Party order is shuffled each time the page loads, so no party is always first.

Up to three quotes per party per topic, in the order the party lists its policies. The first is shown; "Show more" reveals the rest, for every party alike. If a party has fewer than three policies on a topic, we add further commitments from the same pages, in order. Each policy appears once, under the topic it fits best.
Quotes are the party's own words, in quotation marks, cut at about 20 words. '…' marks a cut, and [square brackets] mark words we added for clarity.
A tag shows the type of source: a policy page, the 2026 manifesto, a dated announcement, a long-term policy, or a petition.
Topic order: the four issues New Zealanders rated most important in the Ipsos Issues Monitor (July 2026) come first: cost of living, healthcare, the economy and housing. The rest are alphabetical.

Where topics meet: spending on one service (such as free doctor's visits) stays in that service's topic. Tax changes and overall budget plans (debt, surplus, total spending) go under Tax and government spending. KiwiSaver and retirement savings go under Welfare and superannuation, unless the policy is a tax change. Policies for Māori within a service stay in that service's topic; Te Tiriti o Waitangi covers the Treaty relationship itself, such as settlements, the Waitangi Tribunal, constitutional change, Māori representation and te reo. Energy bills go where the party frames them.
Where a party's policy pages don't cover a topic, we say so. This doesn't mean the party has no view on it.
Not covered on this site: foreign affairs, defence, agriculture and some social issues. See each party's own policy pages.
